## Summary

We will construct a conduct-stage model by constructing participant-level and trial-level sub-models. The trial-level model will allow us to generate a baseline hazard rate for any trial conditional on trial design features. The participant-level model will enable us to modify the baseline hazard rate by applying hazard ratios for participant-level characteristics.

## Partipant-level model

### Data

```{r makedata}
library(tidyverse)

df <- tibble(
  trial_id = paste0("NCT", sample(1000000:9999999, 4)),
  subject_id = paste0("SUBJ", sample(1:10000), 4),
  status = c(1L, 0L, 0L, 1L),
  time = c(26, 3, 21, 26),
  arm_type = c("Placebo", "Active", "Active", "Placebo"),
  age = c(56.8, 72.1, 45.8, 49.3),
  sex = c("M", "M", "F", "M"),
  other_covariates = c("...", "...", "...", "...")
)

df %>% knitr::kable()
```

## Trial-level model

### Data

```{r makedata2}
library(tidyverse)

df <- tibble(
  trial_id = paste0("NCT", sample(1000000:9999999, 4)),
  r = c(25, 10, 73, 91),
  N = c(1000, 500, 2000, 700),
  t = c(26, 52, 36, 12),
  arm_type = c("Placebo", "Active", "Active", "Placebo"),
  blinding = c("Single", "Double", "Triple", "Double"),
  phase = c(3L, 4L, 3L, 3L),
  other_covariates = c("...", "...", "...", "...")
)

df %>% knitr::kable()
```
